base_properties.human_readable: Puritan Textual Re-Indexing (KJV in the New World)

perspectives.label: Puritans in England
perspectives.comment: Prior to emigration, Puritans experienced the KJV as a tool of the English Crown, suppressing dissent.

perspectives.label: Puritan Congregations in New England
perspectives.comment: In the New World, Puritan congregations self-organized and used the KJV for their own purposes, exercising interpretive power.

perspectives.label: Analytical Observer
perspectives.comment: The KJV's role transformed from suppression to self-determination for the Puritans post-emigration, marking a shift in power dynamics and textual interpretation.

omegas.question: To what extent did the Crown directly control KJV interpretation?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical analysis of Crown directives and enforcement actions.
omegas.impact: Determines the extractiveness experienced by the Puritans in England.
omegas.description: Measures the level of control the Crown exercised over KJV interpretation and usage.

omegas.question: How did self-governance in New England affect Puritan interpretation of the KJV?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Compare Puritan sermons and writings from England vs. New England.
omegas.impact: Clarifies the role of self-determination in re-indexing the KJV for Puritan purposes.
omegas.description: Quantifies the effect of self-governance on textual re-interpretation.

commentary.narrative_context: This story tracks the movement of the King James Version (KJV) of the Bible across a geographic 'Exit Option.' In England, the KJV was a tool of the Crown used to suppress Puritan identity (perceived as a Snare). Upon arrival in the New World, Puritans transformed the KJV into a tool for self-determination, reflecting their evolving power dynamics and textual interpretation.
key_agents: Puritans in England: Primary target (powerless/trapped) - suppressed dissent under the Crown.
Puritan Congregations in New England: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) - self-organized and re-indexed the KJV.
English Crown: (institutional/constrained) - Lost control of KJV interpretation after puritan exit.
Anglican Clergy: (institutional/constrained) - Saw their authority challenged by independent Puritan interpretations.
Analytical Observer: Analytical perspective (analytical/analytical) - Analyzes the transformation of the KJV's role.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.6): High prior to emigration, reflecting Crown control; moderated in New England. Suppression (0.7): Significant suppression in England due to Crown control. Theater ratio (0.3): Low theater ratio, as the KJV was central to Puritan religious practice.
commentary.perspectival_gap: Puritans initially experienced the KJV as a snare but later re-indexed it as a rope for their own purposes. The analytical observer recognizes the transformation in the KJV's role across geographical and political contexts.
commentary.directionality_logic: In England, Puritans were victims of the KJV's enforced interpretation, yielding a high 'd' value. In the New World, they became beneficiaries, shifting the 'd' value.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The shift in the KJV's role resolves the mandatrophy. It was initially a tool for Crown control (Snare) but transformed into a tool for self-determination for the Puritans (Rope) due to their geographical exit and subsequent self-governance.
